what_it_does: This paper addresses deep neural network (DNN) accelerators that use bit-serial processing (analyzing one bit at a time rather than whole numbers). When neural network weights are pruned (zeroed out) at the bit level, the resulting data becomes irregularly scattered, causing some processing elements to run out of work while others are overloaded and creating inefficient memory access patterns. The paper proposes identifying patterns in which bits tend to be zeroed together, then optimizing both the algorithm (how weights are compressed) and the hardware (how the accelerator processes these patterns) to balance the workload.
